name: Sunsama
tagline: Daily planner that pulls tasks and calendar into a focused schedule

pricing.notes: Official pricing checked 2026-07-30; listed at $25/month per person monthly and $20/month annually.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 1 user; daily planning, task/calendar integrations, and analytics; no numeric task cap published.
tiers.notes: The top pricing card shows $22/$17; a lower FAQ on the same live page still says $25/$20, so the card values were used.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom seats, security, invoicing, and support.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; 14-day trial with no card; Enterprise custom
pricing.hiddenCosts: Every teammate added to a workspace is placed on the subscription and billed on a prorated basis.

verdictSummary: A daily planning dashboard is not hard, but Sunsama's value is many integrations, careful UX, calendar sync, and habit-forming workflow.
coreLoopDIY: Pull tasks/calendar events, let the user drag tasks into a day plan, track estimates/completion, and run a daily shutdown prompt.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for a planning habit that survives across tools, not a new to-do list.

priorArt.name: Super Productivity
priorArt.desc: Open-source task/time-planning app with local-first workflows.

alternatives.name: FlowSavvy Free
alternatives.desc: It auto-plans unlimited tasks for the next two weeks; priorities and dependencies are how the paid plan gets you.

facts.install: Create a hosted account in the web app or install the iOS or Android app
facts.engines: A deterministic scheduling algorithm; FlowSavvy explicitly says it does not use machine learning to build schedules
facts.dataFormat: Tasks, events, and settings live in FlowSavvy's cloud database and synchronize with connected Google, Outlook, or iCloud calendars; the service currently provides no general calendar import or export
facts.gapVsPaid: FlowSavvy schedules work automatically but lacks Sunsama’s guided daily-planning and shutdown ritual and its broad task-source import workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires an internet connection; calendar synchronization requires OAuth or app-specific credentials

alternatives.name: Super Productivity
alternatives.desc: A local task planner with timeboxes, focus mode and its own stopwatch; less glossy, less interested in your wallet.

facts.install: Use the browser/PWA or install a packaged desktop or mobile build
facts.dataFormat: Tasks, projects, time records, and settings are local-first in browser or app storage; optional synchronization and backups use the user's chosen WebDAV or Dropbox account
facts.gapVsPaid: Super Productivity has timeboxes and focus tools but not Sunsama’s polished guided daily review, shutdown ritual, and external task aggregation.

alternatives.name: Trevor AI Free
alternatives.desc: One calendar gets task-to-time-block planning and some AI suggestions; multiple calendars and deeper automation cost extra.

facts.install: Create a hosted web account and connect one supported calendar; the web app can be installed to a home screen
facts.engines: A private per-user deep-learning scheduling model; some language features use OpenAI, according to Trevor's documentation
facts.dataFormat: Tasks, calendar events, and scheduling state are processed and stored in Trevor's hosted infrastructure, with connected calendar data synchronized through provider APIs
facts.gapVsPaid: Trevor is a lighter web scheduler with one free calendar rather than Sunsama’s deliberate daily-planning ritual and multi-source task workspace.
facts.setupBlocker: No native desktop or mobile app; calendar integrations require OAuth, and the free tier is limited to one calendar account

rejectedAlternatives.name: Amplenote Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Useful free tasks and notes, but external calendar sync is a Pro feature.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Ellie Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Calendar integration and timebox mode are both behind the subscription.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Routine Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free plan has tasks and calendars, but the daily time-blocking loop is paid.

notes: Good high-price target where the answer is not trivially yes because integrations matter.
prompt:
Build me a solo daily planner like Sunsama. Requirements:

- A local web app on localhost:4400: Node + Express + better-sqlite3, server-rendered
  with a little vanilla JS for drag and drop. No frontend framework.
- Today view, two columns: my Google Calendar events (read-only via googleapis, OAuth
  creds in .env) as a timeline, and today's task list beside it.
- Tasks have title, estimate in minutes, project tag, done flag. Quick-add box at the
  top, plus a backlog panel of unplanned tasks I can drag into today.
- Header shows planned minutes vs a daily budget from config (default 6h) and turns
  red when I overplan.
- A /shutdown page for the end of day: walks each unfinished task, one keystroke to
  roll to tomorrow, send to backlog, or drop, then shows planned vs actual.
- Keep per-day history in SQLite so a /week page can show the last 7 days of planned
  vs done.
- Calendar is read-only: never write events. Out of scope: task-tool integrations
  (Todoist, Trello, email), mobile apps, and two-way calendar sync.
- No accounts, no telemetry, everything local except the Google API calls.
- README: Google Cloud console steps for the OAuth client · budget an hour, that
  console is the worst part of this build.
